module_title: First in India (Male & Female) - Constitutional and High-Frequency Facts
introduction: The 'First in India' topic is a core pillar of Static GK, frequently targeted in almost every competitive one-day exam (like SSC, Railways, Bank). This foundational level covers the bedrock constitutional posts, judiciary beginnings, and major historical milestones achieved by Indian men and women post-independence.

core_concepts.title: Constitutional and Political Firsts (Male)
core_concepts.description: The first President of independent India was Dr. Rajendra Prasad, and the first Prime Minister was Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru. The first Vice-President was Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, while the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha was G.V. Mavalankar.

core_concepts.title: Constitutional and Political Firsts (Female)
core_concepts.description: The first female President of India was Pratibha Devisingh Patil, and the first female Prime Minister was Indira Gandhi. Additionally, the first female Governor of any Indian state was Sarojini Naidu (Uttar Pradesh), and the first female Chief Minister was Sucheta Kripalani (Uttar Pradesh).

core_concepts.title: Pioneers in Space and Aviation
core_concepts.description: The first Indian man to travel into space was Squadron Leader Rakesh Sharma (1984). The first woman of Indian origin to go into space was Dr. Kalpana Chawla (1997).

core_concepts.title: Firsts in Administration and Law Enforcement
core_concepts.description: The first Chief Justice of India (CJI) was Justice Harilal J. Kania. India's first female Indian Police Service (IPS) officer was Kiran Bedi, while the first female Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer was Anna Rajam George (later Anna Rajam Malhotra).

important_entities.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
important_entities.significance: The President of the Constituent Assembly and the only individual to serve two full terms as the President of India.

important_entities.name: G.V. Mavalankar
important_entities.significance: Full name: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar. Highly revered as the 'Father of the Lok Sabha'.

important_entities.name: Sarojini Naidu
important_entities.significance: Nicknamed the 'Nightingale of India'. She was also the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress (1925).

important_entities.name: Rakesh Sharma
important_entities.significance: Flew aboard the Soviet spacecraft Soyuz T-11. When asked by PM Indira Gandhi how India looked from space, he famously replied, 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A classic exam trap! The first Governor-General of independent India was Lord Mountbatten (British). However, if the question asks for the first *Indian* Governor-General of independent India, the answer is strictly C. Rajagopalachari.

If asked for the first *woman* President of the Indian National Congress, the answer is Annie Besant (1917, foreign origin). If asked for the first *Indian* woman President, the answer changes to Sarojini Naidu (1925).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Kiran controls the IPS 'Bedi' (shackles), Anna sits on the IAS throne
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Kiran Bedi = First Female IPS | Anna Rajam George = First Female IAS.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions involving the first Lok Sabha Speaker (G.V. Mavalankar) and the first Chief Justice (Harilal J. Kania) appear frequently. Memorize these exact names seamlessly.
